summary: Preliminary review of the supplied, unreviewed packet: it contains CMS facility and quality observations, community estimates, limited source assertions, utilization measures, and one synthetic teaching profile. Findings are candidate evidence, not verified conclusions.

findings.claim: CMS general information identifies Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital (facility 310038) and Saint Peter’s University Hospital (facility 310070) as acute care hospitals in New Brunswick, NJ. The supplied CMS overall ratings are 2 and 3, respectively. For Robert Wood Johnson, CMS reports 8 mortality measures (0 better, 7 no different, 1 worse), 8 safety measures (3 better, 4 no different, 1 worse), and 11 readmission measures (1 better, 6 no different, 4 worse); Saint Peter’s has different measure counts and results as recorded.
limitations: Published CMS observations; both records are unreviewed, and the packet does not provide rating methodology or measure-level detail for these grouped counts.
These ratings do not establish current operational performance.

findings.claim: For 10/01/2024–09/30/2025, the Robert Wood Johnson HCAHPS record reports that 78% of respondents selected “Always” for nurse communication and 5% selected “Sometimes” or “Never”; each record lists 2,393 completed surveys and a 17% response rate.
limitations: These are survey response percentages, not estimates of all patients’ experiences; the response rate is 17%.
The records are unreviewed, and the packet does not explain response weighting or nonresponse effects.

findings.claim: For 10/01/2024–09/30/2025, Robert Wood Johnson’s central line associated bloodstream infection measure records give a lower confidence limit of 0.245 and an upper confidence limit of 0.920, each labeled “Better than the National Benchmark.”
limitations: These are confidence-limit records, not the underlying point estimate or event count; units and the measure’s full calculation details are absent from this packet.
The benchmark labels are reported source fields, not independently verified findings.

findings.claim: CMS classifies Robert Wood Johnson’s emergency department volume as “very high” for 01/01/2024–12/31/2024. The packet also reports a 2024 total of 28 discharges for DRG 003, with average submitted covered charges of 1,076,013.8929, average total payment of 253,492.03571, and average Medicare payment of 176,362.64286.
limitations: The ED volume category is qualitative and supplies no count.
For DRG 003, charges and payment amounts are distinct reported averages; charges are not cost or actual payment. The packet does not specify currency explicitly or explain payment components.

findings.claim: For 07/01/2022–06/30/2025, the hospital return-days records report a score of 46.3 for heart attack patients (denominator 476; number of patients 466) and a score of 17 for heart failure patients (denominator 1,015; number of patients 820). Both records say comparison to the national result is unavailable.
limitations: The packet does not define the score units or provide returned-patient counts, estimates, or national comparison values.
Do not interpret these scores as a raw readmission rate.

findings.claim: Community estimates report colorectal cancer screening among adults aged 45–75 in 2022: age-adjusted prevalence is 59.6% (95% model-based CI 55.7–63.5) for Middlesex County and 49.0% (44.7–53.2) for New Brunswick; crude prevalence is 63.5% (59.6–67.3) and 49.6% (45.3–53.8), respectively. Separate ACS 2017–2021 estimates report age 65+ at 15.1% (MOE 0.1) in Middlesex County and 6.4% (MOE 0.9) in New Brunswick, and households without broadband at 9.4% (MOE 0.6) and 23.3% (MOE 4.4), respectively.
limitations: These are community-level survey or modeled estimates for the stated geographies and periods, not hospital case mix, individual characteristics, or causal effects.

The age-adjusted and crude screening estimates are different measures and should not be conflated. ACS margin-of-error confidence level is not supplied; population context totals are not necessarily measure denominators.
The records are source-extracted but not domain-reviewed.

findings.claim: A New Jersey staffing source description says quarterly reports summarize licensed inpatient-unit staffing ratios, ED daily staffing and patient counts, and respiratory practitioner counts. Its limitation record says the reports aggregate monthly submissions, acuity and layout differ, many professions are omitted, and no Robert Wood Johnson values were collected in this packet. A separate directory assertion states that facility insurance participation does not establish physician participation and that professional fees are billed separately.
limitations: These are limited paraphrases of source material; no actual staffing values, periods, unit-level data, physician-specific participation, or plan-specific details are supplied.
Facility affiliation or participation cannot establish a practitioner’s shift, privileges, or availability.

findings.claim: The packet includes one synthetic teaching profile describing a fictional 22-year-old named Dominic Rivera and a separate RxNorm lookup associating the queried term “metformin” with RxNorm ID 6809. The profile must not be treated as a real patient or as evidence about this hospital; the terminology record itself advises inspecting concepts before clinical use.
limitations: The profile is explicitly synthetic and contains no verified patient-specific clinical truth.
A terminology lookup does not establish a medication order, dose, clinical appropriateness, or patient use.

gaps: The packet cannot establish current staffed or live capacity, unit-level staffing at Robert Wood Johnson, clinician shift coverage, privileges, or real-time availability.
It cannot provide the underlying central-line infection point estimate or event count, explain the return-days score units, or establish current clinical correctness or patient outcomes.
It cannot determine Robert Wood Johnson’s case mix from county or city prevalence, nor link community estimates to hospital patients.
It cannot determine actual cost or actual payment from submitted charges and reported average payment fields.
Most records are unreviewed or source-extracted but not domain-reviewed; supplied identifiers establish traceability, not factual accuracy.

next_acquisitions.requested_data: Bounded, dated Robert Wood Johnson unit-level staffing submissions and licensed/ staffed bed counts, with unit, shift or reporting interval, definitions, missingness, and source documentation; include ED daily staffing and patient counts if available.
next_acquisitions.reason: The packet describes New Jersey staffing report scope but contains no facility-specific values and cannot establish staffed or live capacity.

next_acquisitions.requested_data: Source documentation for the 2024–2025 CLABSI measure point estimate, event and denominator fields, confidence-interval units, and definition of the hospital return-days score and unavailable fields.
next_acquisitions.reason: Clarify what the reported quality values measure and preserve missingness before interpretation.

next_acquisitions.requested_data: CMS dataset documentation for DRG 003 amounts and payment components, plus bounded facility cost or actual payment data if the research question requires those quantities.
next_acquisitions.reason: The packet contains submitted charges and average payment fields, which do not establish costs or actual payments.

next_acquisitions.requested_data: Current, dated facility-specific clinician participation, privilege, and schedule data, with source and scope; plan-specific insurance participation details if needed.
next_acquisitions.reason: The packet’s facility affiliation record and directory assertion do not establish physician participation, privileges, or shift availability.

next_acquisitions.requested_data: Domain-reviewed source documentation and uncertainty/method details for the cited CDC/ACS periods; acquire hospital-specific case-mix data separately only if authorized and available as shareable aggregate data.
next_acquisitions.reason: Community estimates are not hospital case mix and the supplied records are not domain-reviewed.
